To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
changes in osmolarity affect the activity of the sodium-dependent myo-inositol transporter (SMIT), and that this effect is associated with changes in SMIT mRNA level.
osmotic regulation of SMIT mRNA level and activity is a common feature in cells of renal origin and cells of non-renal origin.
osmotic regulation of Na-dependent myo-inositol transport in neural and endothelial cell lines is similar to that in cells of renal origin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of osmotic regulation of SMIT activity and expression in cells from the renal, neural, and endothelial origins.
the role of inositol in osmoregulation and cell volume control.
the role of the sodium myo-inositol cotranporter (SMIT) in regulating cell volume.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
osmotic regulation of SMIT mRNA and activity is a common phenomenon in renal and extrarenal cells.
the regulation of SMIT mRNA level and MI transport by osmolarity is cell type specific.
changes in osmolarity cause a rapid and transient increase in SMIT activity in endothelial cells, and a slower, more prolonged response in neural cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
osmolarity regulates the activity and mRNA levels of SMIT in neural and endothelial cell types.
the regulation of MI transport is cell type specific, and in cells of neural and endothelium origin, hypertonic conditions increase MI transport, whereas hypotonic conditions decrease MI transport.
the regulation of the sodium-dependent myo-inositol transporter (SMIT), the primary route for myo-inosito (MI) uptake in cells, is complex.

osmotic stress regulates MI transport in neural and endothelial cell lines.
